observation.visible_scene: A fixed-camera view of forested mountain ridges at dawn/dusk, with a pale pink sky above a distant flat cloud sea. Dark conifer silhouettes fill the foreground and line the slopes, while a thick river of white fog pours diagonally from the upper-left ridge across the middle of the frame and pools in the lower-right valley. The trees, ridgelines, and the bottom-right watermark logo hold constant positions throughout, indicating the camera is static and only the fog moves.
visible_changes: The broad diagonal fog band persists across the whole segment while its surface ripples and its edges continuously reform, showing slow flow/morphing rather than the band translating as a rigid object.

Thin wisps of fog swirl around the mid-foreground tree cluster on the left, alternately thickening into visible streaks (e.g. around frames 6, 12, 19, 35) and thinning out, indicating localized eddying as the fog passes the trees.
Fog in the lower-right valley and climbing the dark right-hand slope gradually deepens and spreads, with more rising wisps appearing among the trees toward the later frames.
The distant horizon cloud layer and the smooth sheet draping the upper-left ridge remain largely steady, changing only in subtle texture over time.
Foreground tree silhouettes and ridge outlines show no positional change, confirming the motion is entirely within the fog, not the terrain or the camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the fog ultimately clears, rises, or thickens beyond the ~3.3 s excerpt.
The wind or weather conditions driving the flow.
Any change in sun position or overall brightness outside this short window.
uncertain_details: Exact speed and per-parcel direction of the fog are hard to track because adjacent cloud textures look alike.
Whether there is any sub-pixel camera drift is uncertain, though the fixed trees and logo suggest a static shot.
The faint lighting variation between frames is too subtle to confirm as a real change versus compression noise.
